name: Pietro Branca-d'Oro
bio: A young Italian whom Wilde added to his circle in the spring of 1900, between Palermo and Rome. He survives in one sentence to Robert Ross: 'I have added one Pietro Branca-d'Oro to the group. He is dark, and gloomy, and I love him very much.' Wilde had seven months to live.
bio_note: Added 2026-08-06, from the volume's General Index entry 'Branca-d'Oro, Pietro (boy), 1181' - the same '(boy)' form the editors use for Georges, André, Alphonse and Armando. TWO PIETROS, DO NOT MERGE THEM. This map also holds [[pietro]], 'a little Italian, Pietro, like a young St John', met at Nice in January 1899 and recorded at printed 1118. This is a different man: Palermo and Rome, April 1900, printed 1181, and Wilde introduces him as a new arrival - 'I have ADDED one Pietro Branca-d'Oro to the group'. The editors index only this one, under his surname. A name-match against the map would have silently folded them together, which is the same trap [[alphonse]] and [[conway]] presented a day earlier. HE BELONGS TO THE ROME COHORT already added the same day - [[armando]], [[arnaldo]], [[omero]] - and takes it to four. No age is given and none is inferred; the index calls him a boy, Wilde does not.
